Subject: Private-host pilot ask — SparrowHound (initial)

Alex — thanks again for the demo yesterday. SparrowHound wants to run a 6-week pilot of their inference stack using our Private deployment (customer-managed VPC) rather than the hosted API. Key asks from their security and infra team: in-country (US-east) data residency, a shorter audit window (48 hours notice) for forensics, and the ability for their ops team to request limited console access for troubleshooting (timeboxed, read-only).

They are asking for a one-time 15% pilot credit on committed Dedicated pricing to offset onboarding effort. Per our standard, these requests are out-of-policy (audit window & console access). Can you confirm whether we can surface this to deal desk + get an exec exception? I’ve attached the redline MSA and the security questionnaire from SparrowHound.

Quick summary of constraints: 
- Pilot length: 6 weeks, then decide on Reserved Dedicated or Private ongoing
- Residency: us-east (contract clause requested)
- Audit window: 48 hours notice (they requested)
- Console access: read-only, timeboxed with ops SSO (requested)
- Commercial ask: 15% one-time pilot credit

Next steps: if we escalate, I’d like a quick decision today or tomorrow so we can slot them into the on-prem calendar.

Thanks,
Grace

Team — forwarding SparrowHound's ask. They want: in-country residency (us-east), 48-hour forensic notice, timeboxed read-only console access for up to 3 named SparrowHound engineers, and a 15% pilot credit.

Why this matters: they are a strategic AI analytics prospect (target ARR $1.2M in year 1) and the pilot is a quick path to Reserved Dedicated. Operational impact: our infra team will need to reserve a single Private pod for the pilot window and enact KMS key scoping + limited support runbooks. Legal has redlined the MSA and security questionnaire (attached).

Options I see: 
1) Approve limited exception: residency + console access with strict guards (audit logging to their Splunk, just-in-time access, max 48 hours total access per engineer) and offer a 10% pilot credit; require SOC 2 bridge evidence or third-party attestation before pilot start.
2) Deny audit console access and require standard 14-day forensic notice; offer 15% pilot credit if they accept these standard controls.

Asking for your decision (Jonas/Karthik) and any additional commercial guardrails. If we approve, deal desk will finalize discounted quote and operations will schedule the build. HubSpot deal: https://hubspot.redwood.company/deals/DH-2028-0917

Attachments: SparrowHound_MSA_redline.pdf, SparrowHound_Security_Questionnaire.pdf

Thanks — happy to hop on a 15-minute call to walk the tradeoffs.

Grace

Grace — thanks for the clear options and the attachments. I am comfortable approving a narrow exception with the following non-negotiable conditions: 

1) Residency: contractual addendum that enforces US-east data residency for the pilot only; clause expires at pilot end.
2) Concierge console access: allow read-only, JIT access for up to 3 named SparrowHound engineers for troubleshooting only. Access must be granted via their IdP (SAML) and logged; logs must be forwarded to Redwood and to SparrowHound's Splunk instance. Access windows must be pre-scheduled and no single access window may exceed 8 hours.
3) Forensics & audit: reduce notice to 72 hours (compromise from 48). Any emergency forensics outside that window requires a phone call escalation and redwood approval.
4) Commercial: approve a 10% one-time pilot credit (not 15%). We’ll track success metrics in the HubSpot deal and condition further discounts on conversion to Reserved Dedicated.
5) Security gating: SparrowHound must provide a SOC2 bridge or a third-party attestation (no older than 12 months) prior to start.

Operations: Karthik, please confirm we can provision the Private pod for the Sept 4 start and that the requested KMS scoping and Splunk log forwarding are implementable in the pilot timeframe. Marissa, please update pricing in the deal and prepare the one-off quote.

If either of you foresee a hard blocker on the operational side, call me and we’ll reassess. Otherwise, Grace — you have the exec signoff to proceed under the above constraints.
